title: gosec
summary: A public static security checker for Go code.
intended_users: Go developers and CI maintainers finding security weaknesses before release.

design_decisions.problem_or_constraint: Detect varied security weaknesses through static Go analysis.
design_decisions.alternatives_considered: A monolithic scanner is simpler but weakens rule isolation and configuration.
design_decisions.chosen_approach_and_rationale: Separate analyzers, rules, configuration, issue reporting, and command orchestration.
design_decisions.accepted_trade_off: Static analysis has false-positive and false-negative limits.
design_decisions.validation_approach: Review committed rule, analyzer, configuration, and regression tests without execution.
design_decisions.reconsideration_conditions: Revisit boundaries as Go analysis APIs and security classes evolve.

testing_strategy: Committed tests cover rules, analyzers, configuration, and regressions; Finch never executes them.
security_threat: The checker targets concrete insecure code patterns but cannot certify application security.
production_limitation: Static review cannot verify detection accuracy, runtime behavior, or test success.
technical_debt: Deployment-specific tuning and human triage remain necessary.
track_alignment_explanation: Detecting security weaknesses is the product's primary purpose.

ai_disclosure.purposes: No upstream AI-use claim; calibration narrative only.
